summary: José Mendes Cabeçadas (1883–1965) was a naval officer who took the headship of the state and of the government at the end of May 1926, days after the coup of 28 May, and was removed from both in June by Gomes da Costa. He is in the atlas as the first of the three officers who held the presidency in 1926.
